_howto: The Library at datarail.org/library. This file is the source of truth for
the index: the page renders whatever is here and derives its own counts.
Edit it HERE, in fvtale/datarail-library. The copy under
datarail-site/public/library is generated by CI and overwritten on every
publish, so changes made there do not survive.
Entries are added deliberately. A page existing on datarail.org is not by
itself a reason to list it, and some live pages are unlisted on purpose.
Never hand-edit counts anywhere. They are derived.
GROUPS render in the order listed here. 'npm run check' fails on an entry
naming a group that does not exist, so a typo is caught before it ships.
The ids "all" and "github" are reserved.
ENTRY shape - only title, path and group are required:
"title": "Events",
"path":  "/events",
"group": "datarail",
"desc":  "One sentence. What it is, not why it is good.",
"tag":   { "text": "Twice daily", "kind": "live" },
"sub":   [ { "label": "Gelato Academy", "path": "/gelato/courses.html" } ],
"pages": 13,
"keywords": "extra search terms nobody would guess from the title"
tag.kind is "live" (green), "warn" (amber) or omitted (grey).
'pages' is how many pages the entry actually covers, for the total at
the top. Default is 1 plus however many 'sub' links it has. Set it by
hand only for an entry whose sub-pages are too many to list, so the total
still counts them - or, the other way, for a sub link that is a section
of the entry's own page (DocShift's #windows), so one page is not counted
twice.
'keywords' is never displayed - it only widens what the search box
matches. Use it for the word someone would actually type.
An entry may also carry an "app" id, which makes it grantable: an admin
can give an account access to it from the storage console. The id is what
the grant stores, so it must stay put even if the path moves - /BGNYC
became /gelato once, and a path-keyed grant would have broken silently.
"app":    "docshift",
"member": { "path": "/docshift/pro/", "label": "Batch conversion" }
'member' describes the member-only side, and needs an app id to go with it.
Its page can sit on the webspace like any other: what makes it member-only
is that the part worth paying for is fetched from the storage service with
the session cookie and refuses without the grant. A page is not a gate.
The build publishes every entry with an app id to apps.json, which is the
whitelist the admin console reads.
GitHub details are not set here. List the repository in data/repos.json
with "entry" pointing at the entry's path.
Redirect stubs are deliberately not entries. /legiongo, /DAW, /directory and
/STOP1_NYC.html all forward somewhere and are named in the footnote in
site/index.html instead.
